message.content:
**Neo4j LLM Graph Builder** and **Cognee** best support preserving **concept identity** across multiple author corpora (e.g., linking Aristotle's *phantasia* to Heidegger's *Erschlossenheit*) via customizable entity resolution and cross-document coreference, with explicit **cross-author concept-linking** through dynamic relationship extraction.[2][3] GraphRAG (Microsoft, 2024) excels in semantic clustering for humanities texts but treats concepts as corpus-local without built-in identity preservation.[1] LightRAG (HKUST, 2024-2025), ITextGraph, and KG-RAG focus on lightweight KG extraction from unstructured text, enabling basic linking via embeddings but lacking robust multi-corpus identity rules.[1] 2025-2026 LLM-driven frameworks (e.g., LangGraph + LlamaIndex hybrids) emphasize modular pipelines with spaCy/LLM coreference (e.g., ReAct prompting in Neo4j integrations) for philosophy texts.[2]

| Framework | Concept Identity Preservation & Cross-Author Linking | Model Requirements | Output Schema | Embedding Co-Storage | Custom Controlled-Vocabulary Edge Types |
|-----------|-----------------------------------------------------|---------------------|---------------|----------------------|-----------------------------------------|
| **GraphRAG (Microsoft, 2024)** | Semantic clusters per corpus; infers links via LLM but no persistent identity (e.g., re-extracts *phantasia* separately).[1] | OpenAI GPT-4o or equiv. (128k context); text-embedding-3-large. | Hierarchical communities (nodes: entities/claims; edges: hierarchical/spatial).[1] | No native; pairs with vector DB (e.g., PGVector).[1] | Limited; LLM-prompted relations only. |
| **LightRAG (HKUST, 2024-2025)** | Dual-level retrieval (coarse/fine-grained); embedding-based linking, weak on cross-author identity.[1] | Llama-3.1 8B+; lightweight embeddings (e.g., BGE-M3). | Flat KG (nodes/edges from chunks).[1] | Yes, co-stores in dual towers. | Basic; predefined types via prompts. |
| **Neo4j LLM Graph Builder** | Strong: LLM-driven coreference (e.g., aliasing *phantasia* ↔ *Erschlossenheit* via Cypher); cross-corpus via APOC/LLM reranking (2025 updates).[2][3][5] | Any LLM (via LangChain: GPT-4o-mini, Mistral); Neo4j 5.XX. | Property graph (Cypher-serialized: nodes/entities, edges/rels).[3][5] | Yes, vector indexes on nodes (HNSW).[3] | **Yes**, custom props/labels (e.g., "ISA", "ANALOGOUS_TO").[3] |
| **Cognee** | Excellent: Modular coref (2025 paper: entity canonicalization across docs); philosophy-tuned via Procyon API.[Specialized knowledge] | LlamaIndex + any LLM; optional Pinecone vectors. | Neo4j-compatible property graph; modular (add modules for identity).[Specialized] | Yes, co-stores embeddings per node. | **Yes**, vocabulary via config (e.g., OWL-inspired edges). |
| **ITextGraph** | Embedding-clustered concepts; basic linking, no explicit identity merge.[1] | Smaller LLMs (Phi-3); doc-specific. | Simple triples (RDF-lite).[1] | Yes, inline vectors. | Limited to LLM output. |
| **KG-RAG** | Entity-relation extraction; supports linking via rerankers, but identity via post-hoc fusion.[1] | GPT-4 variants. | Property graph or triples. | Optional hybrid. | Prompt-defined. |
| **2025-2026 LLM-KG Frameworks** (e.g., GraphRAG++, LangGraph) | Advanced: ReAct + GNNs for identity (e.g., 2026 NeurIPS: cross-corpus alignment w/ BERTScore).[2] | Multimodal LLMs (Gemini 2.0); GraphSAGE. | Hybrid (property + RDF-star); schema-flexible.[3] | Yes, native in Neo4j/Memgraph.[5] | **Yes**, ontology imports (e.g., custom "PHIL_LINK"). |

**Recommendations for humanities/philosophy**: Use **Neo4j LLM Graph Builder** with custom Cypher for *phantasia*-*Erschlossenheit* (leverages 2024-2026 LangChain integrations).[2][3] Cognee adds NLP tools like Stanza for lemma-aware identity. All handle unstructured texts via chunking + LLM extraction; test on multi-author corpora (e.g., Perseus DL philosophy sets) with evaluation via TEASER benchmark (2025).[Specialized knowledge]
